<pasted_content id="c617">
## User Story
As a user, I want to quickly book another meeting with someone from a past booking so that I do not have to manually re-enter their information.

## User Scenario
When viewing a past booking, the user can choose to book another meeting with the same attendee. The application starts a new booking flow and automatically fills in the attendee's existing name and email. The user can then choose a new date and time and complete the booking normally. The original booking remains unchanged because booking again creates a separate booking rather than rescheduling the previous one.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Add a **"Book Again"** action to past bookings.
2. Clicking "Book Again" starts a new booking flow rather than modifying or rescheduling the original booking.
3. Automatically prefill the previous attendee's:
   - Name
   - Email
4. Allow the user to review or edit the prefilled attendee information before confirming the new booking.
5. Allow the user to select a new available date and time using the existing booking flow.
6. Successfully completing the flow creates a new booking while leaving the original booking unchanged.
7. Add or update tests to verify the rebooking behavior and ensure existing booking and rescheduling functionality continues to work.

## Out of Scope
- Building a People view of previous attendees.
- Displaying meeting counts or previous meeting history.
- Changing the existing rescheduling workflow.
- Automatically selecting a new meeting date or time.

## What does this PR do?

<!-- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Note: Cal.diy is a community-maintained open-source project. Contributions here do NOT flow to Cal.com's production service. -->

This PR adds a "Book again" action to past bookings. Selecting "Book again" opens the existing booking flow for the same event type and pre-fills the previous attendee's name and email. The attendee can edit the pre-filled information and select a new date and time. Completing the flow creates a new booking without modifying the original booking.

This implementation reuses the existing booking flow rather than treating a rebooking as a reschedule.

- Closes #87
- Part of #51

+/**
+ * Builds a public booking page link for the same event type, prefilled with a previous attendee.
+ * Shared by the "Book again" booking action and the People view.
+ * @returns The relative booking link, or null when the event type can no longer be booked by link
+ */
+export function buildBookAgainUrl({
+  eventType,
+  username,
+  attendee,
+}: {
+  eventType: { slug?: string | null; team?: { slug?: string | null } | null } | null | undefined;
+  username?: string | null;
+  attendee: { name: string; email: string };
+}): string | null {
+  const slug = eventType?.slug;
+  if (!slug) return null;
+
+  const teamSlug = eventType.team?.slug;
+  let basePath: string;
+  if (teamSlug) {
+    basePath = `/team/${teamSlug}/${slug}`;
+  } else if (username) {
+    basePath = `/${username}/${slug}`;
+  } else {
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  const urlSearchParams = new URLSearchParams({ name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email });
+  return `${basePath}?${urlSearchParams.toString()}`;
+}

import { isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice } from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib/reschedule/isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice";
import { BookingStatus, SchedulingType } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
import type { ActionType } from "@calcom/ui/components/table";

import { buildBookAgainUrl } from "../../../modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl";
import type { BookingItemProps } from "../types";

export interface BookingActionContext {
  booking: BookingItemProps;
  isUpcoming: boolean;
  isOngoing: boolean;
  isBookingInPast: boolean;
  isCancelled: boolean;
  isConfirmed: boolean;
  isRejected: boolean;
  isPending: boolean;
  isRescheduled: boolean;
  isRecurring: boolean;
  isTabRecurring: boolean;
  isTabUnconfirmed: boolean;
  isDisabledCancelling: boolean;
  isDisabledRescheduling: boolean;
  isCalVideoLocation: boolean;
  showPendingPayment: boolean;
  isAttendee: boolean;
  cardCharged: boolean;
  attendeeList: Array<{
    name: string;
    email: string;
    id: number;
    noShow: boolean;
    phoneNumber: string | null;
  }>;
  getSeatReferenceUid: () => string | undefined;
  t: (key: string) => string;
}

export function getPendingActions(context: BookingActionContext): ActionType[] {
  const { booking, isPending, isTabRecurring, isTabUnconfirmed, isRecurring, showPendingPayment, t } =
    context;

  const actions: ActionType[] = [];

  // For bookings with payment, only confirm if the booking is paid for
  // Original logic: (isPending && !paymentAppData.enabled) || (paymentAppData.enabled && !!paymentAppData.price && booking.paid)
  if ((isPending && !showPendingPayment) || (showPendingPayment && booking.paid)) {
    actions.push({
      id: "confirm",
      bookingUid: booking.uid,
      label: (isTabRecurring || isTabUnconfirmed) && isRecurring ? t("confirm_all") : t("confirm"),
      icon: "check" as const,
      disabled: false, // This would be controlled by mutation state in the component
    });
  }

  actions.push({
    id: "reject",
    label: (isTabRecurring || isTabUnconfirmed) && isRecurring ? t("reject_all") : t("reject"),
    icon: "ban",
    disabled: false, // This would be controlled by mutation state in the component
  });

  return actions;
}

export function getCancelEventAction(context: BookingActionContext): ActionType {
  const { booking, isTabRecurring, isRecurring, t } = context;

  return {
    id: "cancel",
    label: isTabRecurring && isRecurring ? t("cancel_all_remaining") : t("cancel_event"),
    icon: "circle-x",
    color: "destructive",
    disabled: isActionDisabled("cancel", context),
    bookingUid: booking.uid,
  };
}

export function getVideoOptionsActions(context: BookingActionContext): ActionType[] {
  const { booking, isBookingInPast, isConfirmed, isCalVideoLocation, t } = context;

  };

export function getAfterEventActions(context: BookingActionContext): ActionType[] {
  const { booking, isBookingInPast, cardCharged, attendeeList, t } = context;

  // The first attendee is the person who made the booking; the People view offers the others
  const primaryAttendee = attendeeList[0];
  const bookAgainUrl = primaryAttendee
    ? buildBookAgainUrl({
        eventType: booking.eventType,
        username: booking.user?.username,
        attendee: primaryAttendee,
      })
    : null;
  const bookAgainBase = {
    id: "book_again",
    label: t("book_again"),
    icon: "repeat",
    disabled: !isBookingInPast || !bookAgainUrl,
  } as const;
  const bookAgainAction: ActionType = bookAgainUrl
    ? { ...bookAgainBase, href: bookAgainUrl }
    : bookAgainBase;

  const actions: (ActionType | null)[] = [
    bookAgainAction,
    ...getVideoOptionsActions(context),
    booking.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED && booking.paid && booking.payment[0]?.paymentOption === "HOLD"
      ? {
          id: "charge_card",
          label: cardCharged ? t("no_show_fee_charged") : t("collect_no_show_fee"),
          icon: "credit-card",
          disabled: cardCharged,
        }
      : null,
    {
      id: "no_show",
      label:
        attendeeList.length === 1 && attendeeList[0].noShow ? t("unmark_as_no_show") : t("mark_as_no_show"),
      icon: attendeeList.length === 1 && attendeeList[0].noShow ? "eye" : "eye-off",
      disabled: false, // This would be controlled by booking state in the component
    },
  ];

  return actions.filter(Boolean) as ActionType[];
}

export function shouldShowPendingActions(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
  const { isPending, isUpcoming, isCancelled } = context;
  return isPending && isUpcoming && !isCancelled;
}

export function shouldShowEditActions(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
  const { isPending, isTabRecurring, isRecurring, isCancelled } = context;
  return !isPending && !(isTabRecurring && isRecurring) && !isCancelled;
}

export function shouldShowRecurringCancelAction(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
  const { isTabRecurring, isRecurring } = context;
  return isTabRecurring && isRecurring;
}

export function shouldShowIndividualReportButton(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
  const { booking, isPending, isUpcoming, isCancelled, isRejected } = context;
  const hasDropdown = shouldShowEditActions(context);
  return !booking.report && !hasDropdown && (isCancelled || isRejected || (isPending && isUpcoming));
}

    isBookingInPast,
    isDisabledRescheduling,
    isDisabledCancelling,
    isAttendee,
    isCancelled,
    isRejected,
  } = context;

# PR Review: "Book again" for past bookings (commit 8a4c94b7c1)

## Context
Read-only review of the PR closing #87. 5 files, +158/−1: two source files, two test files, one translation key. Nothing to implement. This file holds the review. Any follow-up fixes would be a separate step.

## Systems touched
1. **Booking actions model** (`apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts`)
   - Pure functions (`getPendingActions`, `getEditEventActions`, `getAfterEventActions`, …) build `ActionType[]` from a `BookingActionContext`.
   - The PR adds a `book_again` entry at the top of `getAfterEventActions`. Its `href` comes from the new helper.
   - It is disabled when `!isBookingInPast` or when no URL can be built.
2. **Actions dropdown UI** (`BookingActionsDropdown.tsx`, unchanged)
   - Already shows the "After event" section and passes `href` to `DropdownItem` whenever an item is enabled. So the new action gets a working link with no UI changes.
   - The dropdown's `onClick` mapping falls through to `undefined` for `book_again`, which is correct.
3. **New URL helper** (`apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.ts`)
   - Builds a link to the public booking page:
     - `/team/{teamSlug}/{slug}` for team events
     - `/{username}/{slug}` for personal events
     - `null` when there is no event type or slug (for example dynamic group bookings)
   - Adds `?name=&email=` using `URLSearchParams`.
4. **Booker prefill** (existing, unchanged)
   - `packages/features/bookings/Booker/hooks/useInitialFormValues.ts:136` already reads `email`/`name` from the query string, and they take priority over the logged-in user's values.
   - So the PR reuses the normal booking flow. Nothing touches the reschedule path (`/reschedule/{uid}`). A new booking is created and the original stays unchanged.
5. **i18n**: `"book_again": "Book again"` in `en/common.json`.

## Findings
- **Misleading comments about a "People view" that doesn't exist.** See `buildBookAgainUrl.ts:3` ("Shared by … the People view") and `bookingActions.ts:187` ("the People view offers the others"). No People view exists in the repo, and the issue lists it as out of scope. These look like leftovers from a bigger branch or plan (epic #51), or unreviewed AI output. Remove them or reword them.
- **Only the first attendee is prefilled.** This is documented and reasonable for the AC ("the attendee"). For bookings with several attendees there is no way to pick a different person. Acceptable, but worth noting.
- **Cancelled and rejected past bookings stay enabled.** This is deliberate and tested. A cancelled booking that is still in the future is disabled, which is a bit inconsistent. Minor, and open to debate.
- **Upcoming bookings show a greyed-out "Book again".** This matches the existing pattern (`no_show` is also shown disabled), so it's fine.
- **Deep relative import** `../../../modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl` from `components/`. Small style point; check whether other files use an alias.
- **Awkward `href` construction.** The `as const` base plus a conditional spread is more convoluted than it needs to be. Small readability nit.
- **Test gaps.**
  - The unit tests cover URL building (user, team, encoding, null cases) and the action states (past, upcoming, cancelled, no attendees, no username). They are good and meaningful.
  - Nothing checks that the Booker actually prefills the fields, or that finishing the flow creates a new booking and leaves the original alone (AC 5/6/7). That would need an E2E test, and none was added.
- **PR description.**
  - The summary and test steps are clear.
  - The template placeholder text was left in ("Show screen recordings…", "Add side-by-side screenshots…").
  - The docs checkbox is ticked without writing "N/A".
  - There is no AI disclosure.

## Scores
| Criterion | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness | 8 | Meets AC 1–6 by reusing the Booker's existing query-param prefill. No reschedule coupling. Edge cases (no slug, no username, no attendees) are handled safely. |
| Test coverage | 7 | 11 focused unit tests. No E2E test for prefill or the new booking being created, so AC 7 is only partly met. |
| Code quality | 7 | Small diff that fits the existing action pattern. Comments point to a nonexistent People view, there's a deep relative import, and the href spread is clunky. |
| Documentation | 6 | Clear summary and test steps. Template placeholders left in, docs checkbox not marked N/A, misleading inline comments. |
| AI transparency | 4 | No disclosure. The "People view" references are a sign of output nobody checked. One screenshot shows manual testing. |
| Overall | 7 | Approve after small changes: remove the People-view references and clean up the PR template. An E2E test would be nice to have. |

## Verification (optional, if the user wants it)
- `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.test.ts apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.test.ts`
- The user does the manual check: Past tab → ⋯ → Book again → fields prefilled → book → a new row appears and the original is unchanged.

## Systems changed and how the new code fits

1. **Booking actions** (`apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts`). The bookings list builds its "⋯" menu items from small functions. The PR adds a `book_again` item at the top of the "After event" section. It links to a URL from a new helper and is greyed out when the booking isn't in the past or no URL can be built.
2. **Actions dropdown** (`BookingActionsDropdown.tsx`, unchanged). It already turns an enabled item's `href` into a link, so no UI code was needed.
3. **New helper** (`apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl.ts`). It builds the public booking link: `/team/{teamSlug}/{slug}` for team events, `/{username}/{slug}` for personal ones, and nothing when there's no event type or slug (for example dynamic group bookings). It then adds `?name=…&email=…`.
4. **Booking page prefill** (unchanged). `useInitialFormValues.ts:136` already reads `name` and `email` from the URL, and they win over the logged-in user's details. - **Misleading comments about a "People view".** `buildBookAgainUrl.ts:3` says the helper is "Shared by … the People view", and `bookingActions.ts:187` says "the People view offers the others". No People view exists in the repo, and the issue lists it as out of scope. These look like leftovers from a bigger plan (epic #51) or AI output nobody checked. They should be removed.
- **No end-to-end test.** The 11 unit tests are good: they cover the URL for user and team events, special characters, the cases with no link, and when the item is enabled or disabled. - **Only the first attendee is used.** That's the person who made the booking, which fits the issue, but there's no way to pick someone else on a booking with several attendees.
- **Cancelled bookings are inconsistent.** A cancelled booking in the past gets an enabled "Book again" (on purpose, and tested), but a cancelled one still in the future doesn't. Minor and open to debate.
- **Small style issues.** The import `../../../modules/bookings/lib/buildBookAgainUrl` is a deep relative path. The way `href` is added (an `as const` base plus a conditional spread) is more convoluted than it needs to be.
- **PR description.** The template placeholder text was left in ("Show screen recordings…", "Add side-by-side screenshots…"). The docs checkbox is ticked without writing "N/A". There's no mention of whether AI was used.
